title: 165 Million Tons of Mountain Slid in 90 Seconds and Nobody Got Hurt

scenes.text: 165 million tons of mountain slid down in Utah. Nobody got hurt.
It happened in 2013 at the Bingham Canyon copper mine. Two slides, each lasting about 90 seconds.
The rock travelled nearly two miles. That's enough to bury Central Park 65 feet deep.
It even shook the ground. One of the earthquakes it set off reached magnitude 2.5.
The mine had been evacuated before it fell.
165 million tons. And no one got hurt.

description:
In 2013 a wall of the Bingham Canyon mine in Utah collapsed in two slides of about 90 seconds each, moving roughly 165 million tons of rock.
It is thought to be the largest non-volcanic landslide in North America in modern times, and it triggered small earthquakes. The mine was evacuated beforehand, so nobody was hurt.
How would you spot a landslide before it happens?
first_comment: The pit is more than 3,180 feet deep, the largest artificial hole in the world. Would you work at the bottom of it?
